sources.title: StuartXchange: Santan / Ixora coccinea
sources.limitation: Secondary folklore compilation, not a primary clinical study or safe recipe. Shared Santan names do not identify a cultivar; the genus-only flower-tempura lead remains excluded. No human dose, child use or therapeutic efficacy is established.

sources.title: Gupta and Jain (2011): Investigation of wound healing activity of methanolic extract of stem bark of Mimusops elengi Linn
sources.limitation: Methanol Soxhlet bark extraction and mouse wound experiments are laboratory descriptions only. No human wound remedy, solvent substitution, raw fruit serving process, clinical efficacy or safe dose is adopted.

sources.title: StuartXchange Kabiki: explicit Kabiki/Bansalagin merger warning
sources.limitation: The page explicitly combines historically separate Kabiki and Bansalagin names, folklore and studies. Its merged remedies and aliases are not adopted as exact-species evidence; this is not a modern synonym determination.

retrievals.visualReview: Local Poppler-rendered PNGs read after web screenshots timed out. Rendering warned about Symbol/ArialUnicode fonts; reviewed method text and voucher remained legible. Other PDF pages were not visually checked.

proposals.preparationPart: Roots; not flowers, nectar or an unspecified Ixora cultivar
proposals.preparationDescription: StuartXchange's Ixora coccinea entry reports Philippine traditional use of a root decoction in accounts concerning nausea, hiccups and appetite loss. This secondary folklore description is not a safe home recipe or treatment. No quantities, preparation times, medicinal dose, child-use guidance or clinical efficacy are established by this account.

proposals.preparationPart: Authenticated stem bark; not fruit flesh, seeds or leaves
proposals.preparationDescription: Gupta and Jain's authenticated Mimusops elengi stem-bark study shade-dried and powdered the bark, extracted it with methanol in a Soxhlet apparatus, removed solvent under reduced pressure and incorporated the extract into an ointment base for mouse wound experiments. This laboratory description is not a home recipe or treatment and does not establish a safe human wound-care preparation or dose.

excludedFromAdoption: Experimental extraction quantities, concentrations, duration, treatment frequency and animal wound-induction procedures
Transferring animal findings into human wound care or replacing methanol with a household solvent
Santan infant baths, eye drops, cancer preparations and cultivar-ambiguous flower foods
Merged Kabiki/Bansalagin folklore and aliases as exact-species methods
Reclassifying unspecified Bisayan names as Cebuano
Human efficacy, dosage, clinical review or publication clearance
remainingGaps: Santan's exact-cultivar food preparation and primary traditional source verification remain unresolved.
Kabiki fruit-processing and human bark-use safety remain unresolved despite the laboratory description.
Balibago leaf-food processing and human bark-use safety remain unresolved.
